answer: A lotus and saffron market gives one IPv4 onboarding quota per source /24 network each round, shared by all accounts. A ripple of aliases behind one proxy thus shares one quota. The server uses the connection's observed address, never a submitted header, and completes a nonce exchange before counting a claim. A farm must rent proxies across more networks or control a distributed botnet, adding costs beyond key creation. This coarse subsidy defense penalizes shared networks, needs separate IPv6 policy and cannot stop well-funded proxy farms.
